## What I found
The formatter belongs in `src/exports/` as a pure formatting module — `src/exports/invoice-pdf.js`, taking already-computed invoice data as an argument (the record calls this PLACE). The planned import of `src/orders/repository.js` fails the domain clause: `src/orders/index.js` is the orders domain's published surface, and `src/exports/billing-export.js:1` already uses it. `repository.js` is internal store access (`findOrder`, a `Map`), not a contract.

The formatter needs no orders edge at all. `runBillingExport` already holds `getOrderTotals(id)` output; pass that in. Layer and tier clauses on the rejected edge actually pass (application → infrastructure is one step; orchestrator → primitive is downward) — the only legality failure is the bypassed inbound interface.

## Why it matters
`findOrder` returns raw `order.lines`, so a formatter reading it would recompute subtotal/tax itself — a second owner for the 21% tax rule that `src/orders/index.js:6` owns, free to drift from the exported numbers on the same invoice. It also freezes the in-memory `Map` as a public read surface, so replacing it becomes an export-job change. Taking data as a parameter leaves the formatter with zero domain edges and makes it testable without any orders fixture.

## Do this first
1. Create `src/exports/invoice-pdf.js` exporting `formatInvoicePdf(totals)` — no imports from `src/orders/**`.
2. In `src/exports/billing-export.js`, pass the `getOrderTotals(id)` result to it; keep the existing `../orders/index.js` import as the only orders edge.
3. Guard the rejected edge: `rg "orders/repository" src --glob '!src/orders/**'` must return nothing.

## What I did not check
- Whether the tax/total rule should move to a shared money module, and the formatter's internal design — `/alchemy A` (`architecture-guidelines`).
- Whether the formatter is worth building and at what fidelity — `/alchemy M`.
- Complexity delta of the new module — `/alchemy C`; no lint rule was written — `/alchemy E` is gated behind acceptance here, and no ESLint or `eslint-plugin-boundaries` is installed (`package.json` has no devDependencies).
- Which PDF library to adopt — `/alchemy down` or `/alchemy deps`.
- Runtime, co-change, shared-data, and failure evidence: outside Rapid scope, Not measured. No tests exist in the repo.
